title: Siri Fort Delhi - The Second City of Delhi’s History
content:
Siri Fort - Delhi,

Siri Fort is one of Delhi’s oldest forts, built in the 13th century by Alauddin Khilji, the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty. Located in South Delhi, this fort was constructed as a strong defense against Mongol invasions and later became the heart of the second city of Delhi.

Although much of Siri Fort lies in ruins today, its massive walls, ancient stonework, and scattered remains still tell stories of medieval Delhi’s strength. Walking through its old gates and broken walls gives visitors a chance to imagine how grand and powerful this fort once was.

Nearby, you’ll also find the modern Siri Fort Auditorium, which hosts cultural programs, film screenings, and concerts, making the area a mix of history and contemporary life. The fort itself is surrounded by greenery, providing a quiet escape from Delhi’s busy streets.

Best Time to Visit: Siri Fort is open to visitors every day from sunrise to sunset, with free entry. You can visit any time of the year, but the best season is from October to March, when the weather is perfect for exploring historical monuments.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest station is Green Park (Yellow Line) or Hauz Khas (Yellow Line), both a short rickshaw ride away.
  • By Bus/Auto: Well-connected by buses and autos from South Delhi.
  • By Car: Street parking is available in nearby lanes.

Entry Fee: 

No Entry fee, Free for all visitors.

Travel Tip: Combine your visit with Hauz Khas Fort or Lodi Gardens for a full day of Delhi’s layered history in one trip.
excerpt: Siri Fort in Delhi was built in the 13th century by Alauddin Khilji to protect the city from Mongol invasions. Though mostly in ruins today, its old walls and gateways still reflect Delhi’s medieval past. Located in South Delhi, it offers history lovers a quiet spot to explore
